result.summary: The environment features a marked crosswalk across a wide-radius slip lane that lacks connecting sidewalks or curb ramps, effectively leading pedestrians into a guardrail and dense vegetation. High-speed vehicle geometry combined with significant sightline obstructions from untrimmed trees creates a high-risk scenario for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Dead-end crosswalk
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk terminates at a guardrail and dense vegetation with no connecting sidewalk or paved path.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, where the crosswalk meets the guardrail

hazards.name: High-speed slip lane
hazards.description: The wide-radius turn lane encourages high vehicle speeds through the pedestrian crossing area.
hazards.location_in_image: The curved roadway area where the crosswalk is painted

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Dense vegetation at the corner obscures the view between approaching drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: The wooded area on the right side of the slip lane

interventions.title: Sidewalk and Ramp Installation
interventions.description: Construct continuous sidewalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps to connect the crosswalk to a pedestrian network.

interventions.title: Corner Radius Reduction
interventions.description: Reconstruct the intersection to tighten the turn radius, slowing vehicles and shortening the crossing distance.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim or remove vegetation at the corner to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The image depicts a wide, multi-lane arterial roadway with no visible pedestrian infrastructure, including sidewalks or marked crossings. The environment is highly hostile to pedestrians due to the high-speed road design and lack of any physical separation or safe crossing points.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Infrastructure
hazards.description: Complete absence of sidewalks or designated walking paths along a high-speed roadway.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: A wide, multi-lane road with no median or refuge island, requiring pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic at once.

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Design
hazards.description: Wide lanes and multiple through-lanes encourage high vehicle speeds without any traffic calming or pedestrian protection.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct paved sidewalks on both sides of the road to provide safe, separated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Signalized Pedestrian Crossing
interventions.description: Install a marked crosswalk with a pedestrian-activated signal to provide a safe, designated crossing point.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Construct a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time, reducing exposure.

result.summary: The intersection features a wide multi-lane roadway with marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals, but lacks a median or refuge island. The residential context and long crossing distances suggest a car-oriented design that prioritizes vehicle throughput over pedestrian comfort.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge, increasing exposure time to vehicles.

hazards.name: High-speed geometry
hazards.description: Wide, straight lanes and lack of traffic calming measures encourage higher vehicle speeds in a residential area.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time and provide a safe waiting area.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Program the signals to give pedestrians a walk sign several seconds before vehicles get a green light to increase visibility.

result.summary: The intersection features faded continental-style crosswalks adjacent to multi-family residential housing. While basic crossing infrastructure exists, it lacks signage, signals, and clear sidewalk connectivity, creating a moderate-risk environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk is significantly worn, reducing its visibility to approaching motorists.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signage
hazards.description: There are no signs warning drivers of the pedestrian crossing at this residential intersection.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalks using high-visibility continental or ladder patterns to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install standard pedestrian crossing warning signs (W11-2) on all approaches to the intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to reduce the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.
